item.title: The Muskox – a hardy Ice Age survivor
item.description:
Mammoths and muskoxen once foraged together, and the horned ruminants still roam the Arctic wildernesses in increasing number (video: Fethecat).
A calf out on a walk; though it resembles bison and other bovine, the muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is closer related to sheep and goats (photo: Randy Kokesch).
It is the last species in a linage that emerged in Central Asia over 2 million years ago, and it was a part of the northern “Ice Age” megafauna (art: Jay H. Matternes).
Bulls can reach a shoulder height of 1.5 m (5 ft), a length of 2,5 m (8.2 ft), and a weight up to 410 kg (900 lb). Their thick fur, that allows them to withstand colds below -50°C (-58°F), often makes them appear even larger (photo: David Ho).
Herds with between 8 to 20 members, depending on the time of the year, are formed of both cows and bulls. The life expectancy of adult animals is 12 to 20 years. Against the threat of predators, such as wolves, the adults form a horned wall with their bodies to protect themselves and the calves (photo: Watne Lynch).
Calves are born in April to June after which the rut begins. Then bulls secrete musk from glands [that gives them their name], and fight for sole access to the cows. The bulls butt head and their skulls manage collisions at 40 km/h (25 mph). The sound of the clashes can be heard over great distances (photo: David Swindler).
From ten to two thousand years ago they disappeared outside of North America due to climate change and human hunting (photo from Chauvet Cave: Jean Clottes). In Alaska a herd survived until at least the 1850s, though a last specimen may been shot as late as in the 1890s, leaving populations only in Canada and on Greenland.
In the 20th century muskoxen were reintroduced from their remaining range (red) to new areas (blue). This included Greenland and mainland North America as well as Russia, Arctic Ocean islands, and Norway, from where a herd migrated into Sweden.
With a world population of about 100,000 animals today it is not considered globally threatened. Muskoxen are also held at farms for their fine fur hair (photo: Yuri Smityuk). — — — — — Video #1 source: https://www.reddit.com/r/NatureIsFuckingLit/comments/1rxik0c/musk_ox_giving_the_side_eye_oc/
